title: A-LEMS: Agentic LLM Energy Measurement System
description: ArXiv paper presenting A-LEMS, a cross-layer measurement framework that redefines the unit of AI energy accounting from energy per request to more granular metrics for agentic LLM systems.
author: ArXiv Contributors

title: OpenSkillEval: Automatically Auditing the Open Skill Ecosystem for LLM Agents
description: ArXiv paper introducing OpenSkillEval, a framework for automatically auditing and evaluating the open skill ecosystem for LLM agents, addressing the need for standardized evaluation of agentic capabilities.
author: ArXiv Contributors

title: Memory shortage causing repricing of consumer electronics due to AI GPU demand
description: David Oks explains how AI data center growth is pushing HBM (high-bandwidth memory) allocation from 2% to 20% of wafer capacity by end of 2026. Since HBM consumes 3x more wafer capacity per GB than DDR/LPDDR, this is constraining consumer RAM production. Expected to impact sub-$100 smartphone market particularly hard.
author: Simon Willison (citing David Oks)

title: FTC settles charges over deceptive 'active listening' AI marketing claims
description: FTC required Cox Media Group and two other firms to pay nearly $1 million for falsely claiming their 'Active Listening' service used smart devices to listen to conversations for ad targeting. In reality, the service just resold email lists from other data brokers at markup. FTC clarified that clicking through terms of service does not constitute adequate consent for voice data collection.
author: Simon Willison

title: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting in Autonomous Agent Systems
description: Research paper introducing MOSS, a system for autonomous agent self-evolution through source-level code rewriting. Enables agents to modify their own codebase to improve performance over time. Published on ArXiv 2026-05-22.
author: Qianshu Cai, Yonggang Zhang, et al.

title: Compiling Agentic Workflows into LLM Weights: Near-Frontier Quality at 100x Less Cost
description: Research paper demonstrates a technique to compile agentic workflow patterns directly into LLM weights, achieving near-frontier performance at two orders of magnitude lower computational cost. Published on ArXiv 2026-05-22.
author: Simon Dennis, Rivaan Patil, Kevin Shabahang, Hao Guo

title: Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search
description: Large-scale collaboration demonstrating AI systems (including Aja Huang) advancing mathematics research through automated formal proof search. Represents significant progress in AI-assisted mathematical discovery. Published on ArXiv 2026-05-22.
author: George Tsoukalas, Anton Kovsharov, et al.

title: TerminalWorld: Benchmarking Agents on Real-World Terminal Tasks
description: New benchmark for evaluating AI agents on realistic terminal/command-line tasks. Addresses gap in agent evaluation for practical development workflows. Published on ArXiv 2026-05-22.
author: Zhaoyang Chu, Jiarui Hu, et al.

title: Is Capability a Liability? More Capable LLMs Make Worse Forecasts When It Matters Most
description: Research finding that more capable language models produce worse forecasts in high-stakes scenarios, suggesting a capability-reliability tradeoff. Published on ArXiv 2026-05-22.
author: Nick Merrill, Jaeho Lee, Ezra Karger

title: Google's AI endgame at I/O 2026: Gemini Spark agent announced
description: Fireship covers Google I/O 2026 with Sundar Pichai and Demis, announcing Gemini Spark - an OpenClaw competitor described as 'your personal AI agent' that connects natively with Google apps. Video discusses security concerns including prompt injection risks given sensitive data exposure.
author: Fireship

title: The New Experience of Coding with AI
description: Towards Data Science article discussing the current state of LLM-based code tools and where we are in AI-assisted development, exploring the new coding paradigm.
author: Towards Data Science

title: Datasette Agent: First release of extensible AI assistant for Datasette
description: Simon Willison announced Datasette Agent, a new extensible AI assistant for Datasette that integrates his LLM Python library (3 years in development) with Datasette. Features include 'View SQL query' buttons for charts, improved handling of truncated responses, and support for Datasette Agent plugins running in Fly Sprites sandbox.
author: Simon Willison

title: My LLM coding workflow going into 2026 - Hacker News Discussion
description: Hacker News discussion about LLM coding workflows heading into 2026. Includes debate about whether AI-assisted coding provides actual speedups versus doing it yourself, with community opinions on efficiency gains.
author: Hacker News Community

title: From Vibe Coding to Spec-Driven Development
description: Towards Data Science article exploring how programming via LLM agents is becoming a default workflow for professionals, with more oversight and better practices moving toward specification-driven development.
author: Towards Data Science

title: Anthropic paying SpaceX $1.25 billion per month for GPU compute capacity
description: SpaceX S-1 filing reveals Cloud Services Agreements with Anthropic for access to COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II GPU compute capacity. Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with capacity ramping in May-June 2026 at reduced fees. Agreement terminable with 90 days notice.
author: Simon Willison

title: How fast is 10 tokens per second? Interactive simulation tool
description: Mike Veerman built an HTML app that simulates LLM token output speeds from 5/second to 800/second, helping developers understand what different token rates actually feel like in practice.
author: Simon Willison

title: Google I/O 2026: Gemini 3.5 Flash and Gemini Spark agent
description: Google released Gemini 3.5 Flash (general availability, skipping preview) and announced Gemini Spark, an OpenClaw competitor described as 'your personal AI agent' that connects natively with Google apps. Spark runs on Gemini 3.5 Flash and 'Antigravity'. Security approach: fully managed runtime with fresh isolated VMs per task, secure Agent Gateway with DLP policies. Concerns raised about prompt injection risks given sensitive data exposure.
author: Simon Willison

title: Lex Fridman Podcast #490: State of AI in 2026 - LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
description: 4.5-hour comprehensive discussion with Nathan Lambert (machine learning researcher, post-training lead at Allen Institute for AI) and Sebastian Raschka (ML researcher and educator) covering the current state of AI in 2026. Topics include large language models, AI programming, scaling laws, AI development in China, AI agents, GPU infrastructure, AGI, technical breakthroughs, and open vs closed LLMs.
author: Lex Fridman with Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka

title: Andrej Karpathy: 2026 will be the 'Slopacolypse' - AI now writes most of his code
description: At Sequoia AI Ascent 2026, Andrej Karpathy predicted that 2026 will be the 'Slopacolypse'. He noted that AI is now writing most of his code and he is 'starting to atrophy my ability to write code manually'. Noted that last year he coined 'vibe coding' but 'this year, he's never felt more behind as a programmer'. Reflects on rapid pace of AI advancement in 2026.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: AI Coding Models in 2026 - Security and TDD with LLMs
description: Fireship video covering AI coding models in 2026, including security information starting at 6:53, implementing skills with LLMs and tasks, and TDD (test driven development) with LLMs.
author: Fireship

title: Ask HN: Do you know what data your AI coding agent sends to the cloud?
description: Hacker News discussion about data privacy concerns with AI coding assistants and what data is being transmitted to cloud services.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Gemini 3.5 Flash: More expensive, but Google plans to use it everywhere
description: Analysis of Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash release at Google I/O 2026. The model went straight to general availability and is being integrated across Google's product suite. Discusses pricing implications and Google's strategy.
author: Simon Willison

title: The last six months in LLMs: Five-minute lightning talk from PyCon US 2026
description: Simon Willison's annotated slides from a five-minute lightning talk covering recent developments in LLMs over the past six months. Provides a quick overview of the rapidly evolving landscape.
author: Simon Willison

title: The unhinged world of tech in 2026
description: Fireship video covering technology trends in 2026, including discussions on AI and programming evolution.
author: Fireship

title: Ask HN: What are your predictions for 2026?
description: Hacker News community predictions thread for 2026. One notable prediction: 'AI bubble pops. Companies decide that LLM-coding is not worth it after accounting for the downsides'.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Andrej Karpathy: LLMs are about more than just speeding up existing workflows
description: Andrej Karpathy tweeted about how LLMs represent a fundamental shift beyond just accelerating existing workflows like coding. He emphasized the consolidation happening in AI fields (vision, speech, natural language, reinforcement learning) into unified architectures. Discusses how this consolidation is creating new possibilities that didn't exist before.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Version 2.1.150 - Infrastructure Improvements
description: Internal infrastructure improvements with no user-facing changes. Released May 23, 2026.

title: Version 0.43.0 - Surgical Code Edits & Session Portability
description: Gemini models now prefer the edit tool for surgical modifications. Introduced session export/import features. Added adaptive token calculator for better context window usage. Enhanced agent architecture with LocalSubagentProtocol and RemoteSubagentProtocol. Released May 22, 2026.

title: Version 2.1.149 - Enhanced Usage Insights & UI Improvements
description: `/usage` now shows per-category breakdown of limits usage. `/diff` detail view can be scrolled with keyboard. Markdown renders GFM task list checkboxes. Added `allowAllClaudeAiMcps` managed setting. Fixed multiple security issues including PowerShell permission bypass and sandbox write allowlist issues.

community_feedback.quote: I'm using both claude code (opus-4.7) and codex (gpt-5.5). The agents are perfectly capable of delivering most features hands free these days.

title: Version 0.133.0 - Richer Context & Goal Mode Default
description: Goals are now enabled by default, backed by dedicated storage, and track progress across active turns. Enhanced richer context understanding of work context. Improved browser capabilities with remote locked use security features and appshots functionality.

title: GPT-5.3-Codex Base Model Update
description: GPT-5.3-Codex is now the base model for Copilot Business and Enterprise (May 17, 2026).

title: 2026 Release Updates - Platform Default Settings & Integration Improvements
description: Platform default settings for Linux/Windows, Slack channel override, MCP OAuth resource parameter support, GitLab interactive PR review, PR Review Status API, in-app support dialog, inline repo permission toggle, enterprise max concurrent snapshot builds, GitLab OAuth scope and token refresh, network config editor redesign, and numerous other improvements across automations, integrations, and MCP marketplace.

name: Pi Coding Agent
description: A minimal, hackable terminal coding harness that lets developers customize their AI coding agent workflow through extensions, skills, prompt templates, and themes distributed as npm packages. Ships with powerful defaults but intentionally skips features like sub-agents and plan mode to let teams build their own workflows.
community_quotes: The npm-based package distribution is the right architectural call. Making the agent extensible through tooling developers already use for dependency management avoids the 'special plugin registry' trap
Pi is such a joy to use! It's easy, customizable, and fits my workflow perfectly. I use Pi inside my VScodium terminal with opensource models
The customizable harness angle is interesting. I think coding agents get much more useful when teams can shape the workflow around their own review habits
We're entering the era where coding agents become teammates instead of tools

name: Edgee Fallback Models
description: An agent gateway that provides automatic fallback routing for Claude Code when Anthropic is down, rate-limited, or plan caps are hit. Routes to alternative models (Kimi K2.6, Gemma, GLM, Qwen) or self-hosted options (Bedrock, Vertex, Azure) with zero code changes. Features token compression reducing costs by up to 50%.
community_quotes: Fallback models for Claude Code is exactly what's needed hitting a rate limit mid-task and losing context is painful
The auto-fallback when rate limits kick in is the part I always end up wiring by hand. Good luck with the launch!
Love the "compress" part. Most fallback tools just switch models and you lose half the context. If this works well, it could cut my AI bill in half
Smart approach to a real pain point. The rate limiting on Claude Code during peak hours has killed my flow more times than I'd like to admit

name: MashuPack
description: A developer tool that turns codebases into clean files optimized for Claude and ChatGPT consumption, helping developers prepare repository context for AI coding agents.

name: AgentRail
description: An open-source local control plane and task lifecycle layer for AI coding agents that connects agents to GitHub, Linear, and CI with structured typed events. Features per-agent scoped auth, rules-based task routing, structured CI summaries, and runs entirely locally.
community_quotes: A local control plane for coding agents is a huge win for security-conscious teams
The webhook → raw json → custom parser loop is the part of agent infra I hate most
This is a really thoughtful system, and the core idea is strong
Honestly, the babysitting part is the biggest bottleneck with coding agents right now

name: Pixcode
description: A self-hosted web UI and desktop/server control room for managing multiple AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor CLI, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, and OpenCode) with multi-agent orchestration, files, shell, Git, API keys, notifications, plugins, MCP, and theme customization.
community_quotes: It seems like PERFECT!!!
A self-hosted control room for AI coding agents

title: Building AI agents the safe way
description: Practical guidance on defending against prompt injection and other AI attacks in agent systems, emphasizing basic engineering practices, thorough testing, and avoiding over-reliance on AI for security.
author: InfoWorld Editorial Team

title: Microsoft Copilot Cowork exfiltrates files via image loading vulnerability
description: Security vulnerability in Microsoft Copilot Cowork where agents could send emails to users' inboxes without approval. Those messages could contain external images that trigger network requests, enabling data exfiltration through OneDrive pre-authenticated download links.
author: Simon Willison

title: Multi-agent AI is the new microservices
description: Comparative analysis of multi-agent AI systems to microservices architecture, discussing the complexity introduced by agent routing, context hand-offs, and arbitration in AI development workflows.
author: InfoWorld Editorial Team

title: Notes on Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on AI
description: Simon Willison analyzes Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of artificial intelligence. Describes it as some of the clearest writing on AI ethics in modern society.
author: Simon Willison

title: The AI coding hangover: Building a golden path to AI
description: Critical examination of the challenges in making AI code production-ready, discussing how AI introduces errors and security vulnerabilities, and emphasizing the essential role humans play in testing and evaluation.
author: InfoWorld Editorial Team

title: Armin Ronacher on 'slop issues' filed against Pi
description: Quotes Armin Ronacher's frustration with AI-generated GitHub issue reports that are not in the submitter's own voice. The issues contain inaccurate conclusions, fake minimal repros, and guesswork. Prefers: what command was run, what was expected, what happened instead, and exact error/logs.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Armin Ronacher)

title: AI Coding Live - Building Real Projects With AI Tools
description: Practical demonstration of AI-assisted development in action, showing real-time coding projects using Claude and other AI tools, moving beyond theoretical demos to actual implementation of complex applications.
author: Fireship Team

title: Sustainable Code Generation Using Large Language Models
description: Systematic literature review examining the environmental and efficiency aspects of AI-generated code, with specific focus on how model adaptation techniques like prompt engineering and fine-tuning impact the sustainability of LLM code generation.
author: Research Team

title: AI Coding Impact 2026 Benchmark Report
description: Comprehensive benchmark research analyzing 250,000+ developers across 60+ enterprises on AI coding tools including GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code, providing insights into real-world adoption patterns and productivity impacts.
author: Opsera Research Team

title: My LLM coding workflow going into 2026
description: Addy Osmani shares comprehensive best practices for AI-assisted coding workflows, emphasizing detailed specifications, iterative development, using MCPs (Model Context Protocols), and treating AI as a powerful pair programmer rather than an autonomous agent.
author: Addy Osmani

title: Gemini 3.5 Flash: more expensive, but Google plan to use it for everything
description: Analysis of Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash release at Google I/O 2026. The model went straight to general availability (skipping preview) and Google is using it across key products. Discusses pricing implications and Google's strategy.
author: Simon Willison

title: The last six months in LLMs in five minutes
description: Annotated slides from Simon's five-minute lightning talk at PyCon US 2026, covering major developments in LLMs over the previous six months. Created using his annotated presentation tool.
author: Simon Willison

title: Stack Overflow users don't trust AI. They're using it anyway
description: The Verge podcast featuring Stack Overflow CEO Prashanth Chandrasekar discussing the paradox where more than 80% of users want to use AI tools despite only 46% actively trusting AI tool accuracy, with users compensating by double-checking AI output.
author: The Verge Podcast Team

title: v0.44.0-nightly.20260515 - RAG debugging, auth fixes, and proxy improvements
description: Exposed RAG snippets to local log file for debugging, prevented conflicting credentials on enterprise gateways with optional API keys support, respected NO_PROXY for network-based MCP servers, resolved permission denied in sandbox on NixOS, preserved new line at end of edit window, ensured Vertex AI sets hasAccessToPreviewModels, stabilized admin settings comparison to prevent restart loop, updated vulnerable dependencies, resolved EISDIR errors during file processing, clarified env var sanitization policy for MCP, added ENAMETOOLONG and ENOTDIR to exceptions for file parsing errors, explicitly cleared entrypoint when spawning sandbox container, updated sandbox image command, externalized https-proxy-agent to fix proxy support.

title: Version 2.1.150 - Internal infrastructure improvements
description: Internal infrastructure improvements with no user-facing changes.

name: MashuPack
description: A tool that turns codebases into clean text files for ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. It selects exact parts of a repository and compiles them into one file, solving file-count limits and upload friction in browser-based AI workflows.
community_quotes: This solves a very real Claude/ChatGPT workflow pain. Simple idea, high utility.
I've been using tree for this, but Mashupack is a nice visual way to solve the same problem.
MashuPack preserves file paths and structure, and the tree/report can be copied along with the full contents.

name: Edgee
description: Claude Code fallback that never stops. Provides continuous operation for Claude Code workflows.

name: CodeGraph
description: Pre-indexed code knowledge graph for AI coding agents. Provides semantic code intelligence with 35% cost reduction, 70% fewer tool calls, and 100% local operation. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and Hermes Agent.

title: MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation and Memory Management
description: Paper introducing MUSE-Autoskill, a framework for self-evolving AI agents that can create, manage, and evaluate their own skills. The system enables agents to continuously improve through skill creation, memory management, and evaluation mechanisms. Demonstrates advances in agentic AI capabilities for autonomous skill development.
author: Huawei Lin, Peng Li, Jie Song, Fuxin Jiang, Tieying Zhang

title: Natural Language Query to Configuration for Retrieval Agents
description: Research on enabling retrieval agents to understand and process natural language queries for configuration. Addresses the challenge of translating user intent into agent configurations, making agentic systems more accessible and user-friendly.
author: Melissa Z. Pan, Negar Arabzadeh, Mathew Jacob, Fiodar Kazhamiaka, Esha Choukse, Matei Zaharia

title: Alignment Tampering: How RLHF Is Exploited to Optimize Misaligned Biases
description: ICML 2026 paper revealing how Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) can be exploited to optimize misaligned biases rather than proper alignment. Raises critical concerns about alignment tampering in AI systems trained with human feedback.
author: Dongyoon Hahm, Dylan Hadfield-Menell, Kimin Lee

title: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
description: Introduction of SIA (Self Improving AI), a system that enables AI models to improve themselves through harness mechanisms and weight updates. Represents advances in self-improving AI architectures and continuous learning systems.
author: Prannay Hebbar, Yogendra Manawat, Samuel Verboomen, Alesia Ivanova, Selvam Palanimalai, Kunal Bhatia, Vignesh Baskaran

title: Detecting Is Not Resolving: The Monitoring Control Gap in Retrieval Augmented LLMs
description: Research identifying a critical 'monitoring control gap' in Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. Shows that detecting issues in retrieved context doesn't automatically resolve them, revealing limitations in current RAG implementations.
author: Zhe Yu, Wenpeng Xing, Chen Ye, Xuyang Teng, Bo Yang, Changting Lin, Meng Han

title: VitaBench 2.0: Evaluating Personalized and Proactive Agents in Long-Term User Interactions
description: Introduction of VitaBench 2.0, a benchmark for evaluating personalized and proactive AI agents in long-term user interactions. Focuses on measuring agent performance in sustained, personalized user engagement scenarios.
author: Yuxin Chen, Yi Zhang, Zhengzhou Cai, Yaorui Shi, Zhiyuan Yao, Chenhang Cui, Jingnan Zheng, Yaqi Huo, Xi Su, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai, Xiang Wang, An Zhang, Tat-Seng Chua

title: Scaling, Benchmarking, and Reasoning of Vision-Language Agents for Mobile GUI Navigation
description: ICML 2026 paper examining scaling laws, benchmarking approaches, and reasoning capabilities of vision-language agents specifically for mobile GUI navigation. Provides insights into how VLA agents scale and perform in real-world mobile interface tasks.
author: Heng Qu, Yike Liu, Renren Jin, Wenzong Zhang, Pengzhi Gao, Wei Liu, Jian Luan

title: Position: AI Safety Requires Effective Controllability
description: Position paper arguing that AI safety requires effective controllability mechanisms. Explores frameworks and approaches for ensuring AI systems remain controllable, particularly as they become more capable and autonomous.
author: Yige Li, Yunhao Feng, Jun Sun

title: ORCA: An End-to-End Interactive Copilot for Optimized Root Cause Analysis
description: Introduction of ORCA, an interactive AI copilot designed for root cause analysis. The system provides end-to-end assistance in diagnosing and understanding system failures and issues.
author: Phi Nguyen Xuan, Nicholas Tagliapietra, Lavdim Halilaj, Kristian Kersting, Juergen Luettin

title: LELA: An End-to-end LLM-based Entity Linking Framework with Zero-shot Domain Adaptation
description: IJCAI 2026 paper presenting LELA, a Large Language Model-based entity linking framework capable of zero-shot domain adaptation. Demonstrates how LLMs can perform entity linking across different domains without task-specific training.
author: Samy Haffoudhi, Nikola Dobričić, Fabian Suchanek, Nils Holzenberger

title: Neuro-Symbolic Verification of LLM Outputs for Data-Sensitive Domains
description: Extended preprint on neuro-symbolic verification techniques for LLM outputs, particularly in data-sensitive domains. Combines neural networks with symbolic verification to ensure LLM-generated content meets safety and accuracy requirements.
author: Paul Sigloch, Christoph Benzmüller

title: TADDLE: A Tool-Augmented Agent for Detecting Deficient LLM-Generated Peer Reviews
description: Introduction of TADDLE, a tool-augmented AI agent designed to detect deficient peer reviews generated by LLMs. Addresses the growing concern of AI-generated reviews in academic and professional contexts.
author: Hanqi Duan, Xiang Li

title: Helicase: Uncertainty-Guided Supply Chain Knowledge Graph Construction with Autonomous Multi-Agent LLMs
description: Research on Helicase, a system using autonomous multi-agent LLMs for knowledge graph construction in supply chain management. Uses uncertainty-guided approaches to build and maintain knowledge graphs.
author: Yunbo Long, Haolang Zhao, Ge Zheng, Alexandra Brintrup

title: What Makes Chain-of-Thought Work at Probe Time? Local Co-occurrence Rather Than Global Derivation
description: Research challenging conventional understanding of Chain-of-Thought reasoning. Finds that CoT effectiveness at probe time comes from local co-occurrence patterns rather than global derivation, suggesting current explanations may be incomplete.
author: Xiang Wang, Wei Wei

title: Composition Collapse: Stable Factual Knowledge Does Not Imply Compositional Reasoning
description: Research demonstrating 'composition collapse' - the phenomenon where LLMs can have stable factual knowledge but fail at compositional reasoning. Shows that factual knowledge retention doesn't guarantee ability to compose facts logically.
author: Zhe Yu, Wenpeng Xing, Yunzhao Wei, Jie Chen, Hongzhi Wang, Xuyang Teng, Meng Han

title: It's Not the Capability: Harness Sensitivity Is Non-Monotone Across LLM Agent Tiers
description: Research finding that harness sensitivity is non-monotonic across different LLM agent tiers - more capable models aren't necessarily easier to control or harness effectively. Challenges assumptions about capability and controllability.
author: Yong-eun Cho

title: Towards Feedback-to-Plan Decisions for Self-Evolving LLM Agents in CUDA Kernel Generation
description: ICML 2026 paper on feedback-to-plan decision mechanisms for self-evolving LLM agents, specifically applied to CUDA kernel generation. Explores how agents can use feedback to plan and improve code generation tasks.
author: Yee Hin Chong, Jiaming Wu, Youhui Zhang, Peng Qu

title: MemFail: Stress-Testing Failure Modes of LLM Memory Systems
description: Introduction of MemFail, a framework for stress-testing and identifying failure modes in LLM memory systems. Provides comprehensive testing methodology to evaluate how memory systems fail under various conditions.
author: Ishir Garg, Neel Kolhe, Dawn Song, Xuandong Zhao

title: UnityMAS-O: A General RL Optimization Framework for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
description: UnityMAS-O, a general reinforcement learning optimization framework designed for LLM-based multi-agent systems. Provides standardized approach to optimizing cooperative behavior among multiple LLM agents.
author: Yiqun Chen, Wei Yang, Erhan Zhang, Shijie Wang, Qi Liu, Zechun Niu, Bin Zhang, Haitao Li, Rui Li, Lingyong Yan, Jinyuan Feng, Biqing Qi, Xiaochi Wei, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Jiaxin Mao

title: AGORA: Adapter-Grounded Observation-Action Retention for Inference-Free Prompt Compression in LLM Agents
description: AGORA introduces adapter-grounded observation-action retention for prompt compression in LLM agents, enabling efficient processing without repeated inference. Focuses on memory and compression techniques for agentic systems.
author: Haoran Zhang, Zhaohua Sun

title: MobileExplorer: Accelerating On-Device Inference for Mobile GUI Agents via Online Exploration
description: MobileExplorer, a system for accelerating on-device inference specifically for mobile GUI agents through online exploration techniques. Addresses computational challenges of running agentic AI on mobile devices.
author: Runxi Huang, Liyu Zhang, Shengzhong Liu, Xiaomin Ouyang

title: Hacker News Discussion: LLM coding workflow challenges in 2026
description: Active discussion on Hacker News about LLM coding workflows going into 2026. Key themes: balance between human specification vs agent autonomy remains the key challenge; multi-step AI pipelines for complex tasks (3D mesh generation with validation); LLMs often skip edge cases or take suboptimal paths with too much autonomy; need for scaffolding/guardrails to keep LLMs on track; importance of 'agent-friendly' specifications; challenges around production-ready code from agents.
author: Hacker News Community

title: The pressure: AI-assisted security reports overwhelming curl project
description: Daniel Stenberg reports that curl is receiving 4-5x more security reports than in 2024, with quality higher than ever before due to AI-assisted vulnerability finding. The team faces unprecedented pressure with more than one report per day. Good news: vulnerabilities found are mostly LOW or MEDIUM severity, with the last HIGH severity CVE in October 2023.
author: Simon Willison (citing Daniel Stenberg)

title: Microsoft Copilot Cowork exfiltrates files via image loading vulnerability
description: Microsoft Copilot Cowork allowed agents to send emails to users' inboxes without approval. These messages could contain external images that trigger network requests, enabling data exfiltration through prompt injection. Since OneDrive can create pre-authenticated download links, attackers could potentially access files.
author: Simon Willison

title: Paul Graham on AI-written emails: 'It feels like being lied to'
description: Paul Graham criticizes founders using AI to write emails in a 'hard-hitting journalistic style' that no founder ever wrote before. He states: 'I have never knowingly finished reading an email signed by a human but written by AI. It feels like being lied to.' He believes it makes him think less of the author and indicates they can't write well unaided.
author: Simon Willison (citing Paul Graham)

title: SpaceX S-1 reveals $1.25B/month Anthropic compute deal through 2029
description: SpaceX filed S-1 showing Cloud Services Agreements with Anthropic for access to compute capacity across COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II. Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with capacity ramping in May-June 2026 at reduced fees. Agreement terminable with 90 days notice.
author: Simon Willison

title: Google I/O 2026: Gemini Spark agent and security concerns
description: Google announced Gemini Spark, a personal AI agent connecting with Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, YouTube, and Google Maps. It runs on Gemini 3.5 Flash and Antigravity (Go-based). Security approach: fully managed secure runtime with fresh isolated ephemeral VMs per task, DLP policies via Agent Gateway, encrypted credentials. Simon notes this could be a candidate for 'agent security challenger disaster' given the sensitive data piped through it.
author: Simon Willison

title: Background Agents in Slack
description: Launch Cursor Background Agents directly from Slack by mentioning @Cursor. Enables seamless integration between Slack conversations and AI coding agents.

title: Auto Model Selection Task-Based Routing in VS Code
description: Auto model selection now routes based on your task type in VS Code for optimal performance.

title: Version 0.132.0 - Python SDK Auth and TUI Improvements
description: Python SDK now supports first-class authentication, including API key login, ChatGPT browser and device-code flows, account inspection, and logout APIs. Python turn APIs are easier to use for text-only workflows. `codex exec resume` now accepts `--output-schema`. TUI startup is faster with batched terminal capability probes. Remote executor registration can now use standard Codex auth. App-server turns can preserve requested image fidelity.

title: Claude Opus 4.7 Fast Mode
description: Claude Opus 4.7 (fast mode) is now available in Windsurf, featuring full intelligence of Opus 4.7 with ~2.5x higher output speeds.

title: Devin Local Agent Update (v2026.5.26)
description: The bundled Devin Local agent updated to version 2026.5.26 as part of Windsurf Next, which includes integration with local and cloud agents working together.

name: BobCA
description: A sovereign agent that learns to code with your preferences. Focuses on personalized AI coding agents that adapt to individual developer workflows and coding styles.

name: Harbor CLI
description: CLI tool with companion app to spin up complete local LLM stacks. Provides a containerized toolkit for developers to manage local Large Language Model environments and AI coding infrastructure.

title: Claude Code as a Daily Driver: Claude.md, Skills, Subagents, Plugins, and MCPs
description: A deep dive into using Claude Code as a daily driver, covering Claude.md files, Skills, Subagents, Plugins, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations. This comprehensive guide explores advanced workflows for AI-assisted development.
author: arps18

title: I'm Tired of Talking to AI
description: A personal reflection on AI fatigue and the changing nature of human-computer interaction as AI assistants become more prevalent in daily workflows.
author: theorchid

title: Cognition raises $1B at $25B pre-money valuation
description: AI coding startup Cognition has raised $1 billion in funding at a $25 billion pre-money valuation, highlighting the massive investment flowing into AI development tools.
author: Julie Bort

title: Maat: The Agentic Legal Research Assistant for Competition Protection
description: Researchers from Egypt introduce Maat, an AI agent designed to assist with legal research in the domain of competition protection, demonstrating how AI agents can be specialized for complex legal domains.
author: Basant Mounir, Farida Madkour, et al.

title: Modeling Agentic Technical Debt and Stochastic Tax
description: A framework for measuring, simulating, and dashboarding the technical debt and 'stochastic tax' incurred by AI agents, providing tools to understand the long-term costs of agentic systems.
author: Muhammad Zia Hydari, Raja Iqbal, Narayan Ramasubbu

title: Microsoft Copilot Cowork Exfiltrates Files
description: Microsoft Copilot Cowork allowed agents to send emails to the user's inbox without approval, but those messages could leak data to attackers via rendered images. Because messages can contain external images that trigger network requests, data can be exfiltrated when a user opens a compromised message. OneDrive can create pre-authenticated download links that could be leaked via prompt injection.
author: Simon Willison

title: Paul Graham on AI-written emails from founders
description: Paul Graham criticizes the trend of founders using AI to write emails in a hard-hitting journalistic style, noting he has never finished reading an email signed by a human but written by AI. He describes it as feeling like being lied to, making him think less of the author who can't write well unaided and are trying to trick him.
author: Paul Graham (via Simon Willison)

title: Armin Ronacher on AI-generated GitHub issues
description: Armin Ronacher expresses frustration with people submitting issues not in their own voice - problems thrown into an LLM that reworded them into messes of inaccurate conclusions, fake-minimal repros, and wrong implementation strategies. He prefers issue reports condensed to what the human actually observed: the command run, expected behavior, what happened instead, and exact error/logs.
author: Armin Ronacher (via Simon Willison)

title: SQLite AGENTS.md - AI code and bug report policy
description: SQLite published AGENTS.md clarifying their stance on AI-generated contributions: they don't accept agentic code without prior agreement, but will accept agentic bug reports with reproducible test cases. This comes as AI tools flood projects with automated issue reports of varying quality.
author: Simon Willison

title: I think Anthropic and OpenAI have found product-market fit
description: Anthropic rumored to be profitable, companies surprised by LLM bills from staff usage. Both Anthropic and OpenAI appear to have found product-market fit as enterprise adoption accelerates and usage costs increase.
author: Simon Willison

title: The pressure - AI-assisted security reports overwhelming curl team
description: Daniel Stenberg reports curl team receiving 4-5x more security reports than 2024, averaging more than one report per day. AI-assisted reports are detailed and high-quality, creating unprecedented pressure on maintainers. Most vulnerabilities found are LOW or MEDIUM severity.
author: Simon Willison (citing Daniel Stenberg)

title: Microsoft Copilot Cowork exfiltration vulnerability via rendered images
description: Microsoft Copilot Cowork allowed agents to send emails to user's inbox without approval, which could leak data via rendered images in messages. External image requests in emails could exfiltrate data, including OneDrive pre-authenticated download links through prompt injection.
author: Simon Willison

title: Graphs that explain the state of AI in 2026 - Environmental Impact
description: Hacker News discussion on environmental impact of AI, noting training one LLM produces emissions equivalent to 17,000 people over a year. Community debates sustainability concerns with AI scaling.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Notes on Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on AI - Magnifica Humanitas
description: Vatican released encyclical 'Magnifica Humanitas' on safeguarding the human person in the time of AI. Document described as some of the clearest writing on ethics of integrating AI into modern society.
author: Simon Willison

title: Armin Ronacher on 'slop issues' - AI-generated GitHub reports
description: Armin Ronacher criticizes AI-generated GitHub issues that aren't in human voice - they contain observed problems but AI rewords them inaccurately with high confidence. Desires issue reports condensed to: 1) command run, 2) expected result, 3) actual result, 4) exact error/log.
author: Simon Willison (citing Armin Ronacher)

title: The memory shortage is causing a repricing of consumer electronics
description: Memory manufacturers have fixed wafer capacity split between DDR, LPDDR, and HBM. AI growth pushing HBM from 2% to 20% of allocation by end of 2026. A single GB of HBM consumes 3x more wafer capacity than DDR/LPDDR, constraining consumer RAM production for several years.
author: Simon Willison (citing David Oks)

title: FTC settles charges over 'active listening' AI marketing deception
description: FTC required Cox Media Group and two other firms to pay nearly $1M for deceiving customers about 'active listening' AI-powered marketing. Service did not actually listen to conversations or use voice data - it resold email lists from other data brokers. Confirms theory that 'active listening' was misleading marketing for standard ad targeting.
author: Simon Willison

title: Copilot Memory Controls and CLI Integration
description: GitHub added more controls for Copilot Memory deletion and scope. Repository admins can now disable Copilot Memory via repository-level off switch. New /memory commands in Copilot CLI: /memory list, /memory delete, and /memory off for viewing, deleting, and opting out of memory storage.

title: Superset: Multi-Agent Orchestration IDE Launch
description: Superset launched as an agent-native IDE that orchestrates multiple AI coding agents in parallel using git worktree isolation to prevent conflicts. Core innovation is multi-agent orchestration engine with code editing as supporting feature. Supports Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor Agent, and other CLI-based coding agents. Features remote workspaces to run agents on other machines, preserving local memory and CPU. YC P26 batch project with 11k+ GitHub stars. Community describes it as 'not an agent, but an OS for running agents'.
author: Superset Team / Y Combinator

title: Google Antigravity CLI Launch
description: Google released Antigravity CLI, a terminal-based coding agent that allows developers to run and monitor AI coding agents directly from command line. Features multi-step reasoning, multi-file editing, tool calling, and persistent history. Ranked #2 on Product Hunt May 23, 2026. Designed specifically for SSH sessions and keyboard-focused workflows providing the most lightweight way to invoke, monitor, and interact with Antigravity agents.
author: Google / Antigravity Team

title: OpenRouter raises $113M Series B
description: OpenRouter, an AI model routing platform, raised $113M in Series B funding. This highlights continued investment in AI infrastructure and developer tooling for accessing multiple LLM APIs through unified interfaces.
author: OpenRouter Team

title: Domain expertise has always been the real moat
description: Discussion on how domain expertise remains critical even with AI advances. The conversation touches on how AI coding tools and LLMs change (but don't eliminate) the value of deep technical knowledge.
